hook: An unveiled memorial vanished from Portchester Castle in just five days.

sections.voiceover: An unveiled memorial vanished from Portchester Castle in just five days.
sections.visual_cue: Close up shot of the stone walls at Portchester Castle in Hampshire.

sections.voiceover: On October 9, 2026, a plaque commemorated 2,500 African Caribbean prisoners of war. Castle staff discovered the bronze marker and a gate padlock gone on October 14, 2026. Where did the memorial go?
sections.visual_cue: Archival photo of the plaque unveiling ceremony with staff present.

sections.voiceover: The stolen object marked 230 years since captives arrived in Hampshire.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the Hampshire coastline near Portchester.

sections.voiceover: BBC News and Portsmouth News reported the sudden theft. Investigators searched the historic fortress grounds for clues. Officials confirmed the missing bronze artifact in 1796 history records.
sections.visual_cue: Newspaper clippings from BBC News and Portsmouth News covering the theft.

sections.voiceover: Portchester Castle holds 2,500 missing prisoner records from 1796.
sections.visual_cue: Wide exterior view of Portchester Castle under overcast skies.
